decision_log.decision: Source plan = 2 registered masters (NOT 1 disambiguation-page master)
decision_log.rationale: Per cycle-1 audit BLOCKING fix #1: 'List of English and British monarchs, is a Wikipedia disambiguation page, not a table source. It points separately to List of English monarchs and List of British monarchs, so source_count=1 and operation_type=filter are not correct as stated. Use source_count=2 and operation_type=union+filter.' Cycle-2 confirmation accepted. source_count=2; operation_type=union+filter (NOT just filter).

decision_log.decision: Universe policy = STRICT Wikipedia regular-row policy (excludes disputed claimants + Interregnum)
decision_log.rationale: Per cycle-1 audit BLOCKING fix #3 + cycle-2 policy lock: 'Strict Wikipedia regular-row policy: exclude disputed-claimant sections including Jane, Matilda, Louis, Edgar.' This preserves source_defined claim_type by treating Wikipedia's own structural rendering (main-sequence vs disputed-claimant section) as the universe membership rule. Excluded: Empress Matilda (1141), Lady Jane Grey (1553), Louis VIII of France (1216-1217), Edgar Ætheling (1066); Interregnum 1649-1660 (Lord Protectors Oliver + Richard Cromwell — not monarchs). Alternative 'Conventional royal-sequence policy' (would include Lady Jane Grey + cite supplementary source) was rejected to keep source_defined cleaner without supplementary citation.

Per cycle-2 audit confirmation: 'Include Edward V.' Edward V (April-June 1483, ~78-day reign before disappearance with brother in Tower of London) is in main sequence of List of English monarchs, NOT in disputed-claimant section. Strict-regular-row policy includes him.

decision_log.decision: Philip II of Spain (jure uxoris 1554-1558) INCLUDED in universe; Royal House(s) = 'Habsburg' curator-normalized
decision_log.rationale: Per cycle-2 audit confirmation: Philip II is in main sequence of List of English monarchs (jure uxoris co-king with Mary I). Strict-regular-row policy includes him. Royal House(s) = 'Habsburg' is curator-normalized per cycle-2 audit's staging edit #4 — Wikipedia master lists Philip but does not directly label his Royal House; per-monarch Wikipedia article (Philip II of Spain) classifies him as Habsburg by ancestry. Curator-normalization documented in normalization_decisions; alternative was registering Philip's per-monarch article as a 3rd source (rejected for source-plan minimality).

decision_log.decision: William III and Mary II split into 2 separate rows (NOT 1 joint row)
decision_log.rationale: Per cycle-2 audit confirmation: 'Split Mary II and William III if keeping scalar End of Reign Year.' Mary II = 1689-1694 (died 1694); William III = 1689-1702 (reigned alone 1694-1702 after Mary's death). Two separate PK rows with shared Accession Year 1689 (resolved by Monarch-ASC tiebreak placing Mary II before William III). Mirror precedent: NATO SG / Chief Justices split sovereignty into per-person rows.

decision_log.decision: Split-reign merge: Henry VI (1422-1461 + 1470-1471) and Edward IV (1461-1470 + 1471-1483) each staged as 1 row with first-accession-year + final-end-year
decision_log.rationale: Per cycle-2 audit's required staging edit #1: 'Split-reign merge rule: Henry VI and Edward IV appear in multiple reign segments; stage one PK row per monarch using first accession year and final end year.' Henry VI was deposed by Edward IV 1461, restored 1470, deposed again 1471 (died in Tower 1471) → 1 row 1422-1471. Edward IV reigned 1461-1470, briefly deposed during Henry VI's Readeption, restored 1471-1483 → 1 row 1461-1483. Single PK + scalar Start/End cells preserved per the schema convention. The overlap between Henry VI 1422-1471 and Edward IV 1461-1483 documents shared periods of contested monarchy in the cell values.

decision_log.decision: Anne cross-list merge: 1 row spanning English + British masters (Accession 1702, End 1714)
decision_log.rationale: Per cycle-2 audit's required staging edit #2: 'Anne cross-list merge rule: one row for Anne, accession 1702 from the English list and end 1714 from the British list.' Anne was Queen of England 1702-1707, then Queen of Great Britain 1707-1714 (Acts of Union 1707 created Kingdom of Great Britain with Anne as first British monarch). Single PK row with cross-list merged values: Accession Year 1702 (from English list) + End Year 1714 (from British list).

decision_log.decision: Sort = Accession Year ASC + Monarch ASC alphabetic tiebreak
decision_log.rationale: Per cycle-2 audit's required staging edit #3: 'Add deterministic tie-break: Accession Year ASC, then Monarch ASC.' Resolves 3 same-Accession-Year ties in the staged universe: 1483 (Edward V before Richard III alphabetically); 1689 (Mary II before William III); 1936 (Edward VIII before George VI). Mirror precedent: `films_winning_at_least_8_academy_awards` sort + alphabetical tiebreak.

decision_log.decision: 1066 cutoff (Norman Conquest start; pre-1066 Anglo-Saxon kings excluded)
decision_log.rationale: Per cycle-2 audit confirmation: 'Keep the 1066 cutoff: defensible.' William the Conqueror's 1066 accession is the canonical start of the English monarchical sequence in modern genealogical framings. Pre-1066 Anglo-Saxon kings (Athelstan 925, Edward the Confessor 1042-1066, Harold II Jan-Oct 1066) are out of scope per the standard cutoff (NOT in main sequence of post-1066 List of English monarchs).

decision_log.decision: Charles III incumbent excluded; Elizabeth II is last staged row (End 2022)
decision_log.rationale: Per cycle-2 audit confirmation: 'Keep Charles III excluded: defensible completed-reign window; Elizabeth II is last completed row.' Mirror precedent NATO SG (Rutte excluded as incumbent) + Chief Justices (Roberts excluded as incumbent). When Charles III's reign eventually ends, universe extends from 42 → 43.

decision_log.decision: Royal House(s) cell = free-text (NOT closed categorical)
decision_log.rationale: Per cycle-1 audit BLOCKING fix #3: 'The proposed closed list omits at least Blois and Orange, and possibly Habsburg if Philip is included. George V is also explicitly shown with both Saxe-Coburg and Gotha and Windsor in the British list, so a single closed House value needs a documented split-house convention.' Cycle-2 audit: 'Use Royal House(s) as text, not a tight closed categorical, unless you fully enumerate all edge labels.' Free-text cell handles edge labels: Blois (Stephen), Orange (William III), Habsburg (Philip II), Saxe-Coburg and Gotha + Windsor split (George V 1910-1917-1936). Closed categorical would have required enumerating these + handling George V's split-house — too complex for cell value uniformity.

decision_log.decision: Category = temporal primary + set_filter secondary; operation_type = union+filter
decision_log.rationale: Per cycle-2 audit confirmation: 'query_category: temporal, secondary_category: set_filter, operation_type: union+filter.' Temporal primary because Accession Year is canonical ordering axis (mirror NATO SG / Chief Justices). set_filter secondary because universe is set-filtered to strict-regular-row + completed-reign + 1066-cutoff scope. operation_type = union+filter (NOT just filter) because the source plan combines 2 master lists via union before applying filters.

decision_log.decision: Entity class = people/monarchs (NEW fine-class extending people bucket from 16 → 17)
decision_log.rationale: Per cycle-2 audit confirmation: 'entity_class: people/monarchs.' NEW fine-class within the existing people bucket (joining laureates ×3, scientists ×2, authors ×2, athletes, painters, philosophers, deities, honorees, politicians, astronauts, diplomats, judges). Monarchs are people in a sovereign-state office role — people bucket matches the individual-person framing.

Per cycle-2 audit confirmation: 'domain: History/Monarchy.' History family currently at 4 instances: Politics ×2 (us_presidents_count_by_birth_state + twentieth_century_us_presidents_attributes) + Empires ×1 + Military ×1; this brings History to 5 with NEW Monarchy subdomain.

normalization_decisions.rule: Name verbatim per Wikipedia per-monarch article canonical title (which matches the 2 master lists' row labels in most cases). 42 closed values per cycle-2 audit's verbatim dump. Notable canonical forms: 'William the Conqueror' (NOT 'William I' — Wikipedia article title uses the byname); 'Stephen, King of England' (with disambiguator comma per Wikipedia title); 'John, King of England' (with disambiguator); 'James VI and I' (reflects Scottish + English numbering — James VI of Scotland + James I of England); 'Anne, Queen of Great Britain' (with title disambiguator); 'Queen Victoria' (with title — Wikipedia article title uses 'Queen Victoria' not bare 'Victoria'); 'Philip II of Spain' (NOT 'Philip I of England' — Wikipedia uses Spanish-numbering canonical title; he was Philip I via jure uxoris). Edward V is 'Edward V of England' (with country disambiguator). George VI / Elizabeth II / Charles III need no disambiguation (only one of each).

Integer year of accession to throne per Wikipedia master tables. For split reigns (Henry VI + Edward IV), use first-accession year per cycle-2 audit's required staging edit #1. For Anne cross-listed across English + British masters, use 1702 (her English accession) per cycle-2 audit's required staging edit #2. For William III + Mary II joint sovereignty 1689, both rows share Accession Year 1689 (resolved by Monarch-ASC tiebreak).

Integer year reign ended via death, abdication, deposition, or co-sovereign's death (Mary II 1694). For split reigns (Henry VI + Edward IV), use final-end-year per cycle-2 audit's required staging edit #1. For Anne, End Year = 1714 from British list (her death) per cycle-2 audit's required staging edit #2. Edward V End Year 1483 = same as Accession Year (78-day reign). Charles I End Year 1649 = execution year (NOT Interregnum start). Interregnum 1649-1660 explicitly out of scope (no staged rows for Cromwell era).

Free-text per Wikipedia master tables. Standard values: Normandy / Blois / Plantagenet / Lancaster / York / Tudor / Stuart / Orange / Hanover / Saxe-Coburg and Gotha / Windsor. Edge cases: 'Habsburg' for Philip II of Spain — curator-normalized per cycle-2 audit's staging edit #4 because the 2 master lists do not directly label Philip's Royal House (per-monarch Wikipedia article classifies him as House of Habsburg); 'Saxe-Coburg and Gotha; Windsor' for George V (Wikipedia master shows both labels reflecting his 1917 royal-decree rename from German house name to Windsor during WWI). Semicolon-delim used for split-house multi-value cell (mirror precedent: `films_winning_at_least_8_academy_awards` multi-director cell).

open_questions.question: When Charles III's reign eventually ends, should the instance be re-staged to include him?
open_questions.answer: Yes, when Charles III dies/abdicates, universe extends from 42 → 43+ (or more if multiple successors in benchmark window). Universe is locked to completed-reign monarchs as of 2026-05-19 staging date. temporal_sensitivity=medium reflects this — monarchical transitions are infrequent.

open_questions.question: Why use 'Habsburg' for Philip II of Spain when the 2 master lists don't directly say it?
open_questions.answer: Per cycle-2 audit's required staging edit #4: curator-normalization decision. Per-monarch Wikipedia article (Philip II of Spain) classifies him as House of Habsburg by ancestry; the English monarchs master list documents him jure uxoris with Mary I but does not label his Royal House. The alternative was registering Philip's per-monarch article as a 3rd source (source_count would have become 3) — rejected per source-plan minimality. The single 'Habsburg' curator-normalization is the only cell value in the 42-row × 4-cell staged universe that is NOT directly master-extractive; documented explicitly.

open_questions.question: Why split-reign merge for Henry VI / Edward IV instead of staging multiple rows?
open_questions.answer: Per cycle-2 audit's required staging edit #1: split-reign merge keeps single PK row per monarch with first-accession + final-end. Henry VI was deposed (1461) then restored (1470) then deposed again (1471); Edward IV reigned 1461-1470, briefly deposed during Henry VI's Readeption, restored 1471-1483. The merge convention preserves Monarch PK uniqueness while documenting the overlap period (Henry VI 1422-1471 overlaps Edward IV 1461-1483 = contested decade) via the cell values themselves.

open_questions.question: Why exclude Lady Jane Grey (1553) when she's commonly known?
open_questions.answer: Per cycle-2 audit + strict-Wikipedia-regular-row policy: Lady Jane Grey is listed in 'Disputed claimant' section of List of English monarchs (NOT in main sequence). Strict policy excludes disputed-claimant entries to preserve source_defined claim_type. Alternative 'Conventional royal-sequence policy' would include her but require citing a supplementary source for her in-sequence status — rejected for source-plan minimality. Her exclusion is explicit + documented; conventional readers expecting her may notice the absence, which is the audit-acceptable trade-off for strict source-definedness.

open_questions.question: What about the Empress Matilda (1141)?
open_questions.answer: Same disputed-claimant exclusion as Lady Jane Grey. Wikipedia's List of English monarchs explicitly notes Matilda is 'rarely listed as a monarch'. Strict-regular-row policy excludes her.

open_questions.question: Why William III's Royal House(s) = 'Orange' but not 'Orange-Nassau'?
open_questions.answer: Wikipedia's List of English monarchs uses 'Orange' as the house label in its master table. Per-monarch article (William III of England) uses 'House of Orange-Nassau' as the full house name. Verbatim master-list label preserved per source-extractive principle; the longer form 'Orange-Nassau' is the full historical-genealogical name but not the master-list cell value.

hygiene_findings: HYGIENE (metadata-only): draft.json::db_analog is valid SQL but underspecifies the load-bearing normalization for split reigns (Henry VI 1422-1471 + Edward IV 1461-1483 each have 2 reign segments in the master tables that need MIN/MAX aggregation per the staging convention) and the Anne cross-list merge (her Accession 1702 from English list + End 1714 from British list needs to be combined via the same aggregation). cycle_2_post_staging_repair.task: Apply cycle-1 NON-BLOCKING HYGIENE metadata-only fix
changes_made: draft.json::db_analog extended with explicit aggregation CTE chain to model split-reign + Anne cross-list + George V split-house merges. New SQL: WITH english_monarchs AS (SELECT ... WHERE NOT is_disputed_claimant AND NOT is_interregnum AND accession_year >= 1066), british_monarchs AS (SELECT ... WHERE NOT is_disputed_claimant AND tenure_status = 'completed' AND accession_year <= 2022), unioned AS (SELECT * FROM english_monarchs UNION ALL SELECT * FROM british_monarchs), merged AS (SELECT monarch_name, MIN(accession_year) AS accession_year, MAX(end_of_reign_year) AS end_of_reign_year, STRING_AGG(DISTINCT royal_house, '; ' ORDER BY royal_house) AS royal_house FROM unioned GROUP BY monarch_name) SELECT ... FROM merged ORDER BY accession_year ASC, monarch_name ASC. The CTE chain now explicitly models: (1) filter step (NOT is_disputed_claimant + NOT is_interregnum + completed-reign + 1066-cutoff + ≤2022); (2) UNION ALL of the 2 master lists (preserves duplicates for Henry VI / Edward IV multi-segment + Anne cross-list); (3) GROUP BY monarch_name with MIN(accession) + MAX(end) aggregation (collapses split reigns + Anne to single rows); (4) STRING_AGG(DISTINCT royal_house) (handles George V's split-house Saxe-Coburg + Windsor aggregation); (5) final ORDER BY (Accession ASC + Monarch ASC tiebreak).

No CSV cells, schema, source_urls, source_count, claim_type, category, operation_type, gt_construction, domain, entity class, sort order, or PK changed in cycle-2 — single metadata-only fix to db_analog SQL aggregation specification.
cycle_2_post_staging_repair.deliverable: Cycle-2 hygiene repair complete. db_analog now explicitly models split-reign + cross-list + split-house aggregations. Ready for cycle-2 verification audit.
